records.title: Cell
records.concept: Cell as the basic unit of life
records.definition: A cell is the basic structural and functional unit of living organisms.
key_ideas: Living organisms are composed of one or more cells.
Cells carry out processes necessary for life.
principles: Cell theory describes fundamental relationships between cells and living organisms.
relationships: Cells contain structures that perform specialized functions.
Multicellular organisms contain many interacting cells.
misconceptions: Not all cells have the same structures or functions.
assessment_ideas: Define a cell.
Explain why cells are considered basic units of life.
sources: Standard biological definitions
Cell theory literature

records.title: Motion
records.definition: Motion is a change in the position of an object relative to a chosen reference frame over time.
key_ideas: Motion is described relative to a reference frame.
Different observers can describe the same motion relative to different reference frames.
principles: Motion requires a reference frame for its description.
relationships: Position changes can be described using displacement.
Time and position can be used to describe velocity.
misconceptions: An object can be moving relative to one reference frame and stationary relative to another.
questions: Why does motion depend on a reference frame?
assessment_ideas: Describe whether an object is moving relative to a stated reference frame.
sources: Standard physics definitions

records.title: Algorithm
records.definition: An algorithm is a finite, well-defined sequence of steps or rules for solving a problem or performing a computation.
key_ideas: Algorithms specify procedures for solving problems.
Algorithms should have clearly defined steps.
Algorithms can be represented using text, pseudocode, diagrams, or programs.
principles: A useful algorithm must specify how a problem is transformed from input to desired output.
relationships: Algorithms can be implemented as computer programs.
Different algorithms can solve the same problem with different efficiency.
misconceptions: An algorithm is not necessarily a computer program.
assessment_ideas: Write an algorithm for a simple everyday problem.
Convert a procedure into pseudocode.
sources: Standard computer science definitions

records.title: Natural Numbers
records.definition: Whole numbers used for counting, with convention-dependent inclusion of zero.
principles: Natural numbers can be ordered and counted.
relationships: Natural numbers are part of the integers.
misconceptions: Natural numbers are not the same as all real numbers.
assessment_ideas: Identify natural numbers from a list.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard mathematical definitions

records.title: Integers
records.definition: Positive and negative whole numbers together with zero.
principles: Adding or subtracting integers produces another integer.
relationships: Integers contain the natural numbers and form part of the rational numbers.
misconceptions: A negative number can still have a large absolute value.
assessment_ideas: Place integers correctly on a number line.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard mathematical definitions

records.title: Rational Numbers
records.definition: Numbers that can be expressed as a ratio of two integers with a nonzero denominator.
principles: The denominator of a rational-number fraction cannot be zero.
relationships: Integers are rational numbers; rational numbers are real numbers.
misconceptions: Not every decimal number is rational.
assessment_ideas: Classify numbers as rational or not rational.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard mathematical definitions

records.title: Variables
records.definition: A symbol representing a quantity whose value may be unknown or may change.
principles: An expression can be evaluated after assigning a value to its variable.
relationships: Variables occur in expressions, equations, functions and models.
misconceptions: A variable does not always represent an unknown.
assessment_ideas: Evaluate an expression after substitution.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard algebraic definitions

records.title: Equations
records.definition: A mathematical statement that two expressions have equal values.
principles: Applying the same valid operation to both sides preserves equality.
relationships: Equations use variables and can represent mathematical models.
misconceptions: An equation is not simply an expression.
assessment_ideas: Solve and verify a linear equation.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard algebraic definitions

records.title: Point
records.definition: A point represents a precise location in geometry without length, width or thickness.
principles: Points can be used to define geometric structures.
relationships: Points form lines, shapes and coordinate systems.
misconceptions: A drawn dot is a representation of a mathematical point.
assessment_ideas: Plot points on a coordinate plane.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard geometry definitions

records.title: Angle
records.definition: An angle describes the amount of rotation between two rays sharing a common endpoint.
principles: A full rotation is 360 degrees or 2pi radians.
relationships: Angles occur in triangles, polygons, circles and trigonometry.
misconceptions: An angle represents more than just the visible space between lines.
assessment_ideas: Classify and measure angles.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard geometry definitions

records.title: Triangle
records.definition: A triangle is a polygon with three sides and three interior angles.
principles: The interior angles of a Euclidean triangle sum to 180 degrees.
relationships: Triangles are fundamental to geometry and trigonometry.
misconceptions: Triangles do not need to have equal sides.
assessment_ideas: Classify triangles using sides and angles.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard Euclidean geometry

records.title: Circle
records.definition: A circle is the set of points in a plane that are the same distance from a fixed centre.
principles: Diameter is twice the radius.
Circumference is 2pi times radius.
Area is pi times radius squared.
relationships: Circles connect geometry, trigonometry and coordinate geometry.
misconceptions: Radius and diameter are not the same length.
assessment_ideas: Calculate area and circumference.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard Euclidean geometry

records.title: Data
records.definition: Data are recorded observations, measurements or values collected for analysis or decision-making.
principles: Statistical conclusions depend on the quality and relevance of data.
relationships: Data are central to statistics, science, research and computing.
misconceptions: More data does not automatically mean better data.
assessment_ideas: Organize and classify a dataset.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard statistical definitions

records.title: Arithmetic Mean
records.definition: The arithmetic mean is the sum of numerical observations divided by the number of observations.
principles: Mean equals total value divided by the number of observations.
relationships: Mean is a measure of central tendency alongside median and mode.
misconceptions: The mean does not have to be one of the observed values.
questions: How is the arithmetic mean calculated?
assessment_ideas: Calculate and interpret a dataset mean.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard statistical definitions

records.title: Probability
records.definition: Probability is a numerical measure of how likely an event is to occur.
principles: Probability ranges from 0 to 1 in the standard model.
Impossible events have probability 0 and certain events have probability 1.
relationships: Probability connects mathematics with statistics, risk and decision-making.
examples: A fair coin has probability 1/2 of landing heads.
misconceptions: A probability of 1/2 does not guarantee exactly half of a small number of trials.
assessment_ideas: Calculate probabilities of simple events.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard probability theory

records.title: Limit
records.definition: A limit describes the value a function or sequence approaches as its input approaches a specified value or as an index grows.
principles: Limits provide the foundation for derivatives and integrals.
relationships: Limits connect functions, continuity, derivatives and integrals.
misconceptions: A limit does not always equal the function value at the point.
assessment_ideas: Evaluate basic limits.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions

records.title: Derivative
records.definition: A derivative describes the instantaneous rate of change of a function with respect to its input.
principles: A derivative is defined using a limit of a difference quotient.
relationships: Derivatives connect functions, limits, motion and optimization.
misconceptions: A derivative is not simply the slope of one fixed straight line.
questions: How is a derivative related to a limit?
assessment_ideas: Differentiate basic functions.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; NIST mathematical-functions reference

records.title: Integral
records.definition: An integral is used to represent accumulation and, in definite form, can represent signed area under a curve.
principles: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus connects differentiation and integration.
relationships: Integrals connect derivatives, area, volume and probability.
examples: The integral of x is x^2/2 + C.
misconceptions: An integral is not always simply geometric area above the x-axis.
questions: How are derivatives and integrals connected?
assessment_ideas: Evaluate basic indefinite and definite integrals.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; NIST mathematical-functions reference

records.title: Counting
records.definition: The process of determining how many objects are in a collection by assigning numbers in order.
key_ideas: Each object should be counted once.
The final number represents the quantity.
principles: Counting follows an ordered sequence.
relationships: Counting supports understanding natural numbers.
misconceptions: Counting the same object more than once.
assessment_ideas: Count a collection and state its quantity.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard mathematical definitions

records.title: Addition
records.definition: The arithmetic operation of combining quantities to obtain a sum.
key_ideas: The result is called the sum.
principles: Adding zero leaves a number unchanged.
Order does not change the sum.
relationships: Addition is related to counting and subtraction.
misconceptions: Confusing addition with multiplication.
questions: What happens when quantities are added?
assessment_ideas: Solve numerical and real-world addition problems.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard mathematical definitions

records.title: Division
records.definition: The arithmetic operation of separating a quantity into equal groups or determining how many times one quantity contains another.
principles: Division by zero is undefined.
relationships: Division is the inverse of multiplication.
Division supports fractions and averages.
misconceptions: Thinking division by zero produces zero.
assessment_ideas: Solve division problems and sharing situations.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard mathematical definitions

records.title: Subtraction
records.definition: The arithmetic operation of finding the difference between quantities or removing one quantity from another.
key_ideas: Subtraction can represent taking away or comparing quantities.
principles: Subtracting zero leaves a number unchanged.
relationships: Subtraction is related to addition.
misconceptions: Assuming subtraction is commutative.
assessment_ideas: Solve subtraction problems and comparison situations.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard mathematical definitions

records.title: Multiplication
records.definition: The arithmetic operation of combining equal groups or scaling quantities.
key_ideas: The result is called a product.
principles: Multiplication by one leaves a number unchanged.
Multiplication by zero gives zero.
relationships: Multiplication is related to repeated addition and division.
misconceptions: Confusing multiplication with addition.
assessment_ideas: Solve multiplication problems and grouping situations.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard mathematical definitions

records.title: Fractions
records.definition: Numbers that represent parts of a whole or quantities expressed as a ratio of two integers with a nonzero denominator.
key_ideas: A fraction has a numerator and denominator.
Fractions can represent parts of a whole.
principles: The denominator cannot be zero.
Equivalent fractions represent the same value.
relationships: Fractions are related to division, ratios, decimals and rational numbers.
misconceptions: Assuming a larger denominator always means a larger fraction.
assessment_ideas: Represent and compare fractions.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard mathematical definitions

records.title: Decimals
records.definition: A positional representation of numbers using a decimal point to express whole and fractional parts.
key_ideas: Decimal notation can represent fractional quantities.
principles: Each position to the right of the decimal represents a negative power of ten.
relationships: Decimals are related to fractions, percentages and rational numbers.
misconceptions: Treating decimal digits as independent whole numbers.
assessment_ideas: Convert and compare decimal quantities.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard mathematical definitions

records.title: Ratios
records.definition: A comparison of two quantities by division or equivalent ordered relationships.
key_ideas: Equivalent ratios describe the same relationship.
principles: The order of quantities in a ratio matters.
relationships: Ratios are related to fractions, rates and proportions.
misconceptions: Treating ratios as ordinary sums.
assessment_ideas: Solve ratio comparison problems.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard mathematical definitions

records.title: Proportions
records.definition: An equality between two ratios.
key_ideas: Unknown quantities can be found using proportional relationships.
principles: Equivalent ratios form equal proportions.
relationships: Proportions build on ratios and support percentages and rates.
misconceptions: Assuming any two fractions form a proportion.
assessment_ideas: Solve unknown quantities using proportions.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard mathematical definitions

records.title: Percentages
records.definition: A way of expressing a quantity as a number of parts per hundred.
key_ideas: Percentages can represent proportions and changes.
principles: 100 percent represents the whole quantity.
relationships: Percentages are related to fractions, decimals, ratios and proportions.
misconceptions: Confusing percentage points with percentage change.
assessment_ideas: Calculate percentages of quantities.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard mathematical definitions

records.title: Factors
records.definition: Integers that divide another integer exactly without leaving a remainder.
key_ideas: Every positive integer has at least one and itself as positive factors.
principles: A factor multiplied by its paired factor produces the original number.
relationships: Factors are related to multiplication, divisibility and prime factorization.
misconceptions: Confusing factors with multiples.
assessment_ideas: Find all factors of given integers.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard mathematical definitions

records.title: Multiples
records.definition: Numbers obtained by multiplying a given number by an integer.
key_ideas: Multiples form a sequence generated by multiplication.
A number is a multiple of another when it is their integer product.
principles: Every nonzero integer has infinitely many positive multiples.
relationships: Multiples are related to multiplication, factors and divisibility.
misconceptions: Confusing multiples with factors.
assessment_ideas: List multiples and identify common multiples.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard mathematical definitions

records.title: Prime Numbers
records.definition: Positive integers greater than one that have exactly two positive divisors: one and themselves.
key_ideas: A prime number has exactly two positive divisors.
Two is the only even prime number.
principles: Every integer greater than one can be expressed uniquely as a product of primes, apart from order.
relationships: Prime numbers are related to factors, divisibility and number theory.
misconceptions: Considering 1 a prime number.
assessment_ideas: Identify primes and factor composite numbers.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard mathematical definitions
